oidc_managed.label: OpenID Connect and the Internal URL are managed by your deployment. Update the mounted configuration file and restart Music Assistant to change them.

server_name.label: Server name
server_name.description:
The name of this Music Assistant instance, shown in the UI and announced on the network (e.g. Sendspin). 
Useful when running multiple servers on the same network.

auth_allow_self_registration.label: Allow User Self-Registration
auth_allow_self_registration.description: Allow users to create accounts via Home Assistant OAuth.

oidc_enabled.label: Enable OpenID Connect
oidc_enabled.description: Offer sign-in through an OpenID Connect identity provider such as Authentik, Keycloak or Authelia. Built-in and Home Assistant sign-in remain available.

oidc_name.label: Identity provider name
oidc_name.description: The name shown on the sign-in button, for example Authentik.

oidc_issuer.label: OpenID Connect issuer
oidc_issuer.description: The exact HTTPS issuer identifier from your provider's discovery document, including any trailing slash. Discovery must advertise PKCE S256 and signed ID tokens.

oidc_client_id.label: OpenID Connect client ID
oidc_client_id.description: Register a client using the authorization code flow and the callback URL documented in the webserver README.

oidc_client_secret.label: OpenID Connect client secret
oidc_client_secret.description: The registered client secret. Stored encrypted. Required unless the client authentication method is none.

oidc_token_auth_method.label: Token endpoint authentication
oidc_token_auth_method.description: Must match your registered client. Use client_secret_basic or client_secret_post for a confidential client; none is for a public client using PKCE.

oidc_allow_self_registration.label: Allow OpenID Connect self-registration
oidc_allow_self_registration.description: Allow identities approved by your provider to create Music Assistant accounts. New accounts receive the User role unless group-to-role mapping is configured. Matching usernames or emails never link existing accounts automatically.

oidc_backchannel_logout.label: Accept OpenID Connect logout notifications
oidc_backchannel_logout.description: Let your identity provider end the Music Assistant sessions created through OpenID Connect. Register /auth/oidc/backchannel-logout on this server as the provider's back-channel logout URL. Local password sessions and separately created access tokens are unaffected.

oidc_groups_claim.label: OpenID Connect groups claim
oidc_groups_claim.description: The claim containing a list of group names, usually groups. Used only when group-to-role mapping is configured. Your provider must include it in the ID token or UserInfo response.

oidc_role_mapping.label: OpenID Connect group-to-role mapping
oidc_role_mapping.description: Optional JSON object mapping exact group names to Music Assistant role IDs, for example {"music-admins":"admin","music-users":"user"}. The first matching group wins. Roles are updated at each OIDC sign-in; missing or unmatched groups deny sign-in and end existing OIDC sessions. Leave empty to manage roles locally.

base_url.label: Internal URL
base_url.description:
The URL that Music Assistant shares with devices and apps on your local network. 
Set it yourself when the automatically detected address does not work for them, for example behind a reverse proxy, with a custom hostname or on a server connected to more than one network.

external_url.label: External URL
external_url.description:
The URL where Music Assistant can be reached from the internet, for example through a reverse proxy. 
Used for links shared with guests (e.g. party and quiz QR codes) and, when it uses HTTPS, for casting dashboards. 
Leave empty if this server is not reachable from the internet.

bind_port.label: [%key:common::config_entries::bind_port::label%]
bind_port.description: The TCP port to run the webserver.

webserver_warn.label:
Please note that the webserver is by default unencrypted. Never ever expose the webserver directly to the internet! 

To access Music Assistant from outside your local network, use the Remote Access feature which secures access to your Music Assistant instance without the need to expose your webserver directly. 

Alternatively, you can use a reverse proxy, VPN or enable SSL.

ssl_inactive_warn.label:
SSL/TLS is enabled, but the certificate could not be loaded, so the webserver is still running unencrypted. 

Check the certificate and private key below and use the Verify button to test them. The webserver switches to HTTPS as soon as a valid certificate is saved.

enable_ssl.label: Enable SSL/TLS
enable_ssl.description:
Enable HTTPS by providing an SSL certificate and private key. 
This encrypts all communication with the webserver.

ssl_certificate.label: SSL Certificate
ssl_certificate.description:
Provide your SSL certificate in PEM format. You can either:
- Paste the full contents of your certificate file, or
- Enter an absolute file path (e.g., /ssl/fullchain.pem)

This should include the full certificate chain if applicable.
Both RSA and ECDSA certificates are supported.

ssl_private_key.label: SSL Private Key
ssl_private_key.description:
Provide your SSL private key in PEM format. You can either:
- Paste the full contents of your private key file, or
- Enter an absolute file path (e.g., /ssl/privkey.pem)

Both RSA and ECDSA keys are supported. The key must be unencrypted.
This is securely encrypted and stored.

verify_ssl.label: Verify SSL Certificate
verify_ssl.description: Test your certificate and private key to verify they are valid and match each other.

bind_ip.label: [%key:common::config_entries::bind_ip::label%]
bind_ip.description:
Bind the (web)server to this specific interface. 
Use 0.0.0.0 to bind to all interfaces (both IPv4 and IPv6). 
Set this address for example to a docker-internal network, when you are running a reverse proxy to enhance security and protect outside access to the webinterface and API. 

This is an advanced setting that should normally not be adjusted in regular setups.

manifest.name: Webserver
manifest.description: Configuration of the webserver and API
